name: Back pain
description: Softening ligaments and a growing bump are often behind back pain. Gentle exercise, warm baths, and a supportive pillow can help.

name: Bloating & gas
description: Pregnancy hormones slow digestion, causing bloating, burping, and yes – farting. Smaller, more frequent meals can help ease it.

name: Breasts leaking
description: That's colostrum – your baby's first milk. Your body starts making it during pregnancy, so a little leaking before birth is normal.

name: Breast soreness
description: Tender, sore, or even leaking breasts are all normal. It's your body getting ready to breastfeed your baby.

name: Constipation
description: Rising progesterone slows your digestive system, which can lead to constipation during pregnancy.

name: Contractions
description: Braxton Hicks (or “practice”) contractions often start in the second or third trimester. It's your body getting ready for labour.

name: Cramping
description: Cramping can often be eased with warm baths, gentle movement, or lying on the side opposite the pain.

name: Dizzy & lightheaded
description: Hormones relax your blood vessels and send more blood to your baby, which can lower blood pressure and leave you feeling faint.

name: Fatigue
description: Feeling wiped out? Fatigue is common, especially in the first and third trimesters, thanks to hormones and disrupted sleep.

name: Food aversions
description: Can't face salad? Chicken giving you the ick? Hormones are rewiring your sense of taste and smell – it's very common.

name: Food cravings
description: Pickled onions? Baked beans and salad cream? Cravings are common in pregnancy, and they can be pretty specific.

name: Frequent urination
description: Needing to pee more often? Hormones and your growing womb pressing on your bladder are usually behind it.

name: Headaches
description: Resting in a quiet, dim room and using warm or cold compresses can help ease pregnancy headaches.

name: Heartburn & indigestion
description: Eating smaller meals, skipping spicy foods, and sipping peppermint tea can help ease heartburn and indigestion.

name: Itching
description: Itching is common in pregnancy - it affects about 20% of pregnant women. It's often caused by stretching or dry skin.

name: Mood changes
description: Rising oestrogen and progesterone can leave you anxious one minute and fine the next. It can feel like a lot.

name: Nausea
description: Around 80% of mums-to-be have nausea or vomiting (morning sickness). Hormone shifts are usually the main cause.

name: Pelvic pain
description: The hormone relaxin loosens your pelvic ligaments for birth, but that movement can cause pain – from a dull ache to sharp twinges.

name: Shortness of breath
description: Feeling out of breath? Your growing uterus presses on your lungs, so it can feel harder to catch your breath.

name: Skin, hair & nail changes
description: Hormone changes can affect your skin, hair, and nails – think stretch marks, acne, visible veins, or melasma.

name: Sleep issues
description: Insomnia, restless legs, vivid dreams, and a bladder that won't quit – pregnancy can make good sleep hard to come by.

name: Spotting
description: Light spotting can be normal early in pregnancy, but it's always worth checking with your midwife or GP.

name: Strong sense of smell
description: A super-sensitive sense of smell affects about two-thirds of pregnancies, probably thanks to hormone changes.

name: Stuffy nose
description: Feeling blocked up? Hormone changes can swell your nasal passages, making congestion a common pregnancy symptom.

name: Sweating
description: Feeling warmer than usual? Totally normal. Increased blood flow in pregnancy can leave your skin feeling extra warm.

name: Swelling
description: Drinking plenty of fluids, putting your feet up, and wearing compression socks can help ease swelling in your feet and ankles.

name: Vaginal discharge
description: Vaginal discharge often increases during pregnancy because your body is producing more oestrogen.

name: Vomiting
description: Being sick? You're not alone. Vomiting is common in pregnancy – but if you can't keep anything down, call your GP or midwife.

name: Other
description: Not every symptom has a neat label. Log what you're experiencing and talk to your midwife if you need help making sense of it.
